dossier.public_summary: The dip repeats on the target star but odd and even dips are very different and exactly twice as deep every second eclipse, and its 0.608-day period is exactly half the star's 1.213-day spot rotation. Depths also change strongly between transits and sectors. This is an eclipsing binary synchronized with the star's rotation, not a planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even eclipses differ by 70.7 sigma with depths differing by 73270 ppm (60% of depth) and even exactly 2.5x odd, classic eclipsing binary at twice the 0.608 d period (period_x2 1.22 d).

Dip period is exactly half the stellar rotation period - dip repeats at a multiple of rotation, same as the variable phase curve (amplitude_ppm 4675, chi2 119.6 dof 9) - rather than at 0.203 d, shows spot systematics dominate.
reasons.value: rotation 1.213 d (sector 29 1.213 d, sector 2 0.203 d alias) vs signal_period 0.608 d, signal_over_rotation 0.5013050288540808

reasons.why: Individual transit and sector depths are highly inconsistent, from real changes not calibration, inconsistent with a planet's constant depth. Flat bottom (v_sigma -15.39, size 12.2 Rearth, rp_over_rstar 0.3033) alone is also reproduced by stellar eclipses, as is on_target centroid.
